newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Carter Holt opens j/v plant in Thailand.
newsitem.headline: Carter Holt opens j/v plant in Thailand.

text.p: Carter Holt Harvey Ltd is to open a joint venture timber truss manufacturing plant in Thailand today, the company said on Wednesday.
The high-tech plant, known as the TG Laserbuilt, is a 50/50 joint venture between Carter Holt Harvey and Thai Gypsum Products Public Company Ltd, a leading Asian building materials manufacturer.
Under the joint venture, which was signed last December, Carter Holt will provide technology expertise and the raw timber resource.
"Thai Gypsum brings extensive distribution and marketing capabilities in Asia, along with broad building products expertise," Carter said in a statement.
Carter's wood products chief executive Peter Springford said New Zealand had an enormous resource of wood, which would double in the next decade.
"Finding markets for our wood products will be increasingly important and cooperative joint ventures like this one are the way of the future, particularly in Asia," he said.
Located north of Bangkok, TG Laserbuilt will produce about 5,000 units a year for housing systems marketed by Thai Gypsum. Around 1.3 million new houses are built in Thailand annually.
Springford said Thailand was still a relatively small market for New Zealand wood products, importing around 6,000 cubic metres annually.
"Our aim is to increase that to around 150,000 cubic metres by 1999," he said.

Springford said Thailand had historically been a significant consumer of wood products, but domestic supplies had dried up in recent times. Demand had been met through imported timber, mainly Asian hardwoods, but those sources were declining and New Zealand was well placed to fill the gap.
